span.p: removedAt set — soft-deleted row, status value preserved

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
submit() resolves the media row first — an unknown or trashed
mediaCode is 404 CORRECTION_NOT_FOUND — and copies its createdBy
into recordCreatedBy, which is what forwarding later targets.
The submitter follows every transition drawn here through
GET /api/corrections/me and /me/{id} (own rows, removedAt IS NULL).
Someone else's row throws IllegalAdminOperationException
CORRECTION_NOT_YOURS — 409 only through GlobalExceptionHandler,
which advises the user package; this controller sits under
platform, where ApiExceptionHandler's catch-all answers 500.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The class-level hasRole('ADMIN') on AdminGuestCorrectionAPI does
not compose with the method annotations: Spring evaluates the most
specific @PreAuthorize only, and SecurityConfig asks /api/** for
authentication alone — so an EMPLOYEE granted correction:update
passes these edges without ROLE_ADMIN.
adminForward() sends an INFO-severity UserWarning to
dto.targetEmployeeId; an id matching no User throws
IllegalAdminOperationException EMPLOYEE_NOT_FOUND and the status
stays put. With no id it falls back to the User named by
recordCreatedBy — that lookup can miss silently, leaving the row
FORWARDED with no warning sent at all.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
adminApply() writes suggestedValue onto the media row first, via a
per-media-type switch over plain string columns; a field outside it
(tags, keywords, genres, and contributors on AUDIO) throws
IllegalArgumentException, 400, and the status is untouched —
TEXT.contributors and VIDEO/IMAGE.contributor do apply.
Terminal covers status only: forward or reject on RESOLVED is 409,
forward, resolve or apply on REJECTED is 409, and a repeat /reject
is a silent no-op — 200, row and audit log unchanged.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DELETE works from any of the four statuses (the unlabelled edges).
adminRemove() only stamps removedAt/removedBy — status unchanged,
and a second DELETE returns 204 with no new audit row.
The row then leaves GET /api/corrections/me and every mutation
lookup (findByIdAndRemovedAtIsNull, 404 CORRECTION_NOT_FOUND);
admins still read it via GET /api/admin/corrections/{id}, a plain
findById, or the search with includeRemoved=true.
